title: mixed-workload-tail-latency-journal-2025-11-03
summary: Weekly performance sync covering a persistent tail-latency regression observed under mixed small/large request workloads after the recent batching heuristic change. We ran focused smoke and soak tests across GPU types, isolated KV cache and network queuing as candidate causes, and sketched an experiment matrix for root cause + mitigations.
content:
Attendees: Aisha P., Benji M., Sanjay R., Evelyn C., Marisol G.

Purpose: capture notes from the 2025-11-03 perf sync and the follow-up triage runs (2025-11-04). This doc collects hypotheses, experiment results, and next actions so the team can iterate quickly.

Observed problem (recap):
- Since batching-heuristic v2 (deployed 2025-10-29), we see a reproducible increase in 99.9th percentile latency for mixed workloads (50% short chat < 64 tokens, 50% long generation ~1600 tokens).
- Baseline prior to the change: p99.9 ~ 420ms. After change: p99.9 spikes to 1.2–1.6s in steady-state at 500 qps. p50/p95 largely unchanged.
- Repro on both T4 and A10p nodes in staging; magnitude larger on older kernels.

Quick sanity checks performed (2025-11-03):
1) Replay of production-like trace (trace-id: perf-replay-2025-11-03-01) against canary cluster without the new batching heuristic -> tail latency back to baseline.
2) Replay with heuristic turned on but forced batch size cap = 8 -> partial improvement (p99.9 down to ~800–900ms).
3) Isolated single-model tests (long-only and short-only mixes): long-only sees no regression; short-only sees no regression.

Preliminary hypothesis list:
- H1: Adaptive batching interacts poorly with KV cache hot/cold transitions, creating occasional stalls when a request triggers cache fill + larger batch assemble.
- H2: Scheduling microqueueing combined with the new heuristic allows a long request to monopolize a GPU slot in an unexpected codepath, delaying many small requests queued behind it (head-of-line blocking inside the runtime).
- H3: Network burst/TCB windowing: when batches cross packet boundaries we get micro-retransmits increasing tail. Reproduced only on one cloud region during early tests (possible noisy NIC driver).
- H4: Edge quantization fallback path is slower and is sometimes chosen for long requests under heuristic (rare, but observed in a small fraction of traces).

Experiment matrix we ran (high-level):
- Matrix axes: batching_heuristic{v1,v2,gradual}, batch_cap{8,16,32}, kv_cache_policy{aggressive,conservative}, preload_kv{true,false}, workload_mix{short-only,long-only,50-50}.
- Node types: T4 (staging-1), A10p (staging-3).
- Jobs: perf-smoke-mixed-2025-11-03-a .. perf-soak-mixed-2025-11-04-d. See linked artifacts for CI IDs.

Key results (selected):
- With batching_heuristic=v2 + batch_cap=32 + kv_cache=aggressive -> p99.9 = 1.45s (worst).
- With batching_heuristic=v2 + batch_cap=8 + kv_cache=conservative -> p99.9 = 650ms.
- With batching_heuristic=gradual (rolling up batch size over 50ms window) + kv_cache=conservative -> p99.9 ~ 480ms (close to baseline).
- Forcing preload_kv=true reduced variance but didn't eliminate spikes; suggests cache fill timing amplifies but not sole cause.

Trace snippets and root cause clues:
- Sample trace perf-replay-2025-11-03-01: small request queued at t=0.0s, waiting 220ms for batch to form, long request enters and triggers kernel switch at t=220ms; small request then experiences 1.1s stall while kernel completes long request.
- Kernel-level logs show a path where long requests flip to a slow attention kernel when effective sequence length estimate overshoots quantization threshold; the heuristic sometimes mispredicts sequence length when prefix tokens are streaming in.

Immediate mitigations tested: 
- Short-term: reduce default batch_cap from 32->8 for mixed workloads (config rollout in staging). Marked as low-risk and reverted quickly once load normalized.
- Medium-term: implement 'short-request fast-path' that prioritizes small requests for the next runtime patch (PR 1429). This preserves batching benefits for large ones while guaranteeing max queuing latency for small.
- Network: opened a cloud ticket to rule out NIC jitter on region staging-3 (ticket ID included in linked_artifacts).

Open action items (owners and ETA):
- Aisha: finalize the 'short-request fast-path' design doc and bench harness by 2025-11-07. (Design doc draft in repo PR 1431).
- Benji: run extended 24h soak with batching_heuristic=gradual and batch_cap=8 across T4 + A10p (job: perf-soak-mixed-2025-11-05). Report on p99.9 variance by 2025-11-06.
- Sanjay: add deterministic tracepoint around kernel selection to help identify mispredictions; instrument and rollout to canary (target 2025-11-10).
- Evelyn: coordinate with SRE/network team to collect NIC-level metrics from staging-3; correlate to perf spikes (SLA: 2025-11-06).
- Marisol: update CI smoke tests to include a 50/50 mixed workload scenario and p99.9 assertion for repo-level checks (PR coming 2025-11-06).

Risks and tradeoffs discussed:
- Lowering batch_cap reduces throughput and increases per-token cost; acceptable short-term but not long-term.
- Fast-path complexity may add maintenance surface and slightly reduce model throughput for pathological workloads; must be gated behind feature flag and A/B tested.

Notes to follow-ups:
- Collect a labeled corpus of affected traces (example IDs listed in linked artifacts) and attach to the confluence investigation page.
- Consider adding a server-side estimate TTL for sequence-length predictions to avoid switching kernels mid-batch.
- Revisit quantization fallback heuristics; add counters when fallback taken to detect correlation with tail spikes.

Meeting appendix: commands and synthetic driver config used for reproductions
- driver: tools/perf-driver run --config tests/mixed-50-50.yaml --nodes t4-staging-1 --qps 500 --duration 10m --record-traces perf-replay-2025-11-03-01
- sample config fragment: workload_mix: [short:0.5,long:0.5], batching.heuristic: v2, batching.cap: 32, kv_cache.preload: false

Closing notes: next sync scheduled 2025-11-07 standup (quick kickoff at 09:30 PST) to review soak results and the A/B plan for the fast-path rollout. Please add any missing traces to the linked artifacts list and flag critical regressions in JIRA-INF-2781.
